title: Mara and the Archive
premise: Sebastian Ashgrove, an insurance investigator who documents the slow, unclaimed collapse of the colony world Meridian, is summoned when a deep-space vessel returns with its crew biologically younger than when they left. The ship carries a fragment of the Archive — a quantum memory lattice that rewrites time and identity for those it touches — and Sebastian discovers his own missing years are written inside it. Pursued by the consortium that engineered the colony's death to hide the Archive's theft, he races across dead space to the last relay, where he must choose between restoring his erased past and broadcasting the truth that will free what remains of Meridian. He burns his own history as the price of the signal, ending the novel as a stranger with a clean record and a colony that finally remembers.
about_author: Sable Brightwater is a former maritime insurance clerk who spent a decade writing loss reports before turning them into fiction. She writes science fiction about paperwork, grief, and the machinery of forgetting from a coastal town that keeps losing its records to the sea.

chapters.title: The Actuary of Small Disasters
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He files his 400th report on Meridian's decay: failing oxygen recyclers no one will pay to fix. Establishes his ritual of recording what others abandon. Emotional beat: weary devotion to a dying place nobody claims.

chapters.title: Return Velocity
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The freighter Halcyon docks eleven years after vanishing; its crew is younger than their departure photos. One survivor, Ilsa Voss, recognizes Sebastian by name though they've never met. Beat: uncanny dread beneath bureaucratic routine.

chapters.title: Claim Number Zero
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She describes the Archive fragment aboard her ship and how it 'unwrote' their aging — and insists Sebastian signed its manifest in a year he has no memory of. Beat: vertigo of being known by your own erased past.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He digs into Meridian's founding records and finds his own signature dated three years before his arrival on-world. The consortium's auditor, Crane, arrives asking polite questions. Beat: paranoia tightening like a form being filled out.

chapters.title: What the Recyclers Remember
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She and Sebastian trace the colony's failures to deliberate supply diversions; the deaths were amortized, scheduled, profitable. First glimpse of the conspiracy's ledger logic. Beat: cold fury at murder by spreadsheet.

chapters.title: Crane's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Crane offers him a transfer off-world and quiet erasure of his impossible records — a bribe shaped like kindness. Sebastian refuses; that night his apartment burns. Beat: the cost of saying no made literal.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Year
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The Archive fragment resonates near Sebastian, replaying fragments of his lost year: a laboratory, a woman's voice, his own hands doing something terrible. Beat: horror at the self he can't verify.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Halcyon
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They find the true manifest hidden in cargo code: the Archive was stolen from the relay at the edge of dead space, and the crew were meant to be its disposable couriers. Beat: purpose crystallizing into a destination.

chapters.title: Debtors' Orbit
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. To steal a ship they must out-negotiate Meridian's debt holders; Sebastian weaponizes his investigator's knowledge of their fraudulent claims against them. Beat: triumph of small competence over institutional power.

chapters.title: Departure Without Clearance
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A brutal launch under fire from consortium security; one ally, dockmaster Oyelaran, stays behind to cover them and is arrested. Beat: guilt as fuel, escape tasting like abandonment.

chapters.title: Dead Space Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The crossing begins; the Archive fragment whispers to both of them differently, showing each the memories they most want. Trust frays as they doubt what's real. Beat: intimacy poisoned by unreliability.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Lattice
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The fragment resolves the voice: Dr. Amara Sen, the Archive's designer, who sealed part of herself in it — and who Sebastian apparently helped imprison there during his lost year. Beat: self-loathing confronting evidence.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Consortium hunters board them mid-void; a tense standoff where Crane, aboard, reveals the colony's death was priced against the Archive's value. Sebastian records everything. Beat: righteous documentation as resistance.

chapters.title: Counterclaim
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian turns Crane's own liability framework against him, forcing a stalemate and buying passage onward — but Crane plants a tracker and a seed of doubt about Ilsa's loyalty. Beat: victory shadowed by betrayal's possibility.

chapters.title: Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. They reach the derelict relay station and find it inhabited by descendants of the Archive's original staff, living in the dark, waiting. Beat: awe and unease — the past kept alive unnaturally.

chapters.title: The Keepers of Amara Sen
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The Keepers reveal the full Archive: every stolen year, every unwritten person, including Sebastian's complete lost self. He must decide whether to read it. Beat: temptation at its purest.

chapters.title: Reading the Missing Man
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He reads his own year: he betrayed Sen under coercion, then chose erasure as penance. Grief and self-forgiveness collide. Beat: the theme of identity resolved inwardly — he accepts being the sum of his worst act.

chapters.title: Crane's Arrival
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Consortium forces hit the relay; the Keepers fall defending the core; Crane demands the Archive be surrendered for 'stewardship.' Ilsa buys Sebastian time with her life hanging in the balance. Beat: sacrifice amid collapse.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Climax. To send the truth through the relay, the Archive must consume a complete identity as fuel. Sebastian feeds it his entire recorded self — reports, memories, name. Beat: triumphant annihilation.

chapters.title: Signal, Falling
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The broadcast reaches Meridian and every colony screen; the ledgers of the dead go public; consortium ships turn back rather than be witnessed. Crane flees into dead space. Beat: catharsis — truth as unstoppable payload.

chapters.title: A Stranger With Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Awake with no past but the story others tell him, Sebastian returns to Meridian, where survivors are rebuilding and Ilsa vouches for the man she watched choose. Beat: quiet rebirth, identity rebuilt from witness.

chapters.title: Mara and the Archive
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, coda. She begins writing the account we've read, naming it after the Keeper child who first called the lattice 'Mara.' The colony remembers; the record continues. Beat: inheritance fulfilled — story as the only archive that survives.
